# Traditional Tests {#testimate-chapter}

As you have read in previous chapters, 
we are super enthusiastic about using randomization approaches to inference. 
Nevertheless, there are some situations 
(such as when reading a scientific journal)
where it may be useful to know about
traditional "frequentist" tests and estimates. 

This chapter gives you the briefest possible introduction to 
`testimate`, a CODAP plugin that performs these traditional tests. 
You'll find it in the **Plugins** menu under **Statistical Inference**.

When you want to know more, [see this guide to the plugin](https://codap.xyz/guides/testimate/000-index.html){target="_blank"}.

The live example below is all set up for you to perform a test. 
We see NHANES data on 20 individuals, including `BMI` and `Sex`. 
Is the mean BMI the same for the two genders? 
The graph suggests that females have a higher mean value.

1. Drag the outcome variable `BMI` from the table into the test,
where is says **drop attribute here**.
A test appears, testing whether BMI could be zero.
Answer: no way. We move on.
1. Drag the predictor, `Sex`, to the right-hand spot in the test.
The test does not change, but a menu appears, 
because more tests are available now.
1. Use the menu to change the test to **difference of means**.
Now we see a P-value of about 0.04.
1. Play with the various controls! Do a one-way ANOVA!
Change the data and see the test update!
